proposed_english: the Tamr (= the Bound One, tentative)
rationale: Unidentified Manichaean technical term in the cosmic ascent-chain (line 1-2): [X] → ⲡⲧⲁⲙⲣ → Answer → Call → Mind → Pillar → First Man → Ambassador → Aeons. Position below the Answer suggests a low cosmic stage, possibly the captive light/soul. Best etymological guess: ⲡⲧⲁⲙⲏⲣ̄ qualitative 'the bound one' from ⲙⲟⲩⲣ. Confidence low; flagged for parallels in subsequent kephalaia.

Greek loanword νοερόν 'intellectual, noeric.' Used here as gloss/equivalent for ⲡⲛⲟⲩⲥ ⲉⲧⲥⲁⲧϥ̄ 'the chosen Mind' — the text itself equates them. Standard Greek philosophical register; retained as 'Noeric' to preserve technical specificity.

Lyc. ⲟⲩⲱϣⲃⲉ = Sah. ⲟⲩⲱϣⲃ 'answer, respond.' Manichaean technical term — the cosmic Answer (cf. ⲡⲥⲱⲧⲙⲉ 'the Hearing/Answer' in glossary; same pair). Capitalized as personified cosmic principle paired with ⲡⲧⲱϩⲙⲉ 'the Call.'

Garment-decoration term in chapter 72 title (line 10) and body (line 19). Possibly cognate with ⲕⲗⲉⲕⲗⲱⲕ 'round, pearl-like.' Forms a triad with ⲥⲗⲁⲡⲗⲉⲡ and ⲛⲱⲧⲏⲛ ⲛ̄ⲣ̄ϩⲱϥ as objects of mystical/typological exposition. Confidence low.
Reduplicated form, paired with ⲧⲁⲕⲗⲉⲕ as a kind of jewel/ornament cluster on garments. Etymology unclear; possibly 'fragments' or 'beads.' Confidence low.

Specialized robe-decoration term modifying ⲛⲱⲧⲏⲛ 'robes' (lines 11-12, 19-20). Etymology unclear; possibly related to ⲣⲱⲕϩ 'burn' (scorched/embroidered pattern), to ⲗⲏⲃϣ 'covering,' or a Lyc. textile term. Left untranslated pending parallels.

Compound title in line 22-23: ⲡⲥⲁⲭⲛⲉ ('the counsel,' fourth of the five faculties per glossary) + ⲙ̄ⲡⲱⲛϩ̄ 'of life.' Standard Manichaean technical term, here listed alongside 'cross/element of light' as a mystical name applied to certain cosmic figures.

proposed_english: the cross of light / the cross of the Light
rationale: Greek loan σταυρός + 'of the light.' Standard Manichaean technical term — the cosmic Cross of Light upon which the Living Soul is suspended throughout matter. Distinct from the historical crucifix; refers to the cosmological dispersion-pattern of light-substance.
